cues.en: you can use lockstep also called deterministic or input passing methods. This is what Halo's campaign and firefight networking use.
cues.zh: 你可以采用锁步（Lockstep），也叫确定性方法或输入传递法。《光环》（Halo）的战役模式和枪火对决模式用的就是这种网络机制。

cues.en: In this model you rely on the complete determinism of your game loop, you pass the non deterministic player controller inputs over the wire and voila, everyone is running in the same game simulation.
cues.zh: 在这种模型下，你完全依赖游戏循环的确定性，只需通过网络传输非确定性的玩家手柄输入，瞧，大家运行的都是完全相同的游戏模拟。

cues.en: The downsides to this are that your input latency from the controller to the game
cues.zh: 但它的缺点在于，手柄到游戏的输入延迟

cues.en: includes the network round trip time
cues.zh: 包含了网络往返时间，

cues.en: to the post of the game.

cues.en: This means that for first person shooters you end up with significant input latency when you try to shoot your gun or jump or operate on the world in any way. Unacceptable in a multiplayer context where players are

cues.en: you can always send all of the network state about your game.

cues.en: Specifically, can always send it atomically.

cues.en: What this means is you will not have problems where the network state of one object is out of sync with the network state of another. You can guarantee that remote clients will receive the entire network state of the world in a consistent way. This fixes an enormous class of bugs. The Quake three model is famous for this.
cues.zh: 这意味着你不会遇到一个对象的网络状态与另一个对象不同步的问题。你能保证远端客户端以一致的方式接收整个游戏世界的网络状态。这解决了一大类 Bug，Quake 3 的模型就是因此而闻名。

cues.zh: 只要你能把游戏的全部网络状态控制在（比方说）几百字节以内，这种做法就极其有效。

cues.zh: 复制是我们在 Bungie 使用的一个术语。我没在其他地方听过这种用法，但很可能也有。它具体指的是：取一台机器上存在的某种状态，然后通过网络传输足够的信息，使其能在另一台机器上被复制。

cues.zh: 这讲的是谁是主机，谁对对象拥有权威。对几乎所有对象、几乎所有东西，因为我们是主机-客户端游戏，而且我们对作弊非常敏感

cues.en: and to attack surfaces for cheating, the host has almost all the authority in our game. He's authoritative over
cues.zh: 对作弊的攻击面也很敏感，主机在我们的游戏里拥有几乎所有的权威。主机对

cues.en: object health, damage events,
cues.zh: 对象的生命值、伤害事件、

cues.en: projectile positions, things like that. Clients can exert some limited authority over their own bipeds and we'll talk about that as well.
cues.zh: 投射物位置之类的东西有权威。客户端可以对自己的双足角色行使一些有限的权威，我们也会讲到这一点。

cues.en: Thirdly,
cues.zh: 第三，

cues.en: prediction.
cues.zh: 预测。

cues.en: Prediction is what you do in between receiving updates about an object. In this little animation I've got here if you assume that this moving circle is an object and this is a simulation occurring on a client machine
cues.zh: 预测就是你在两次收到某个对象的更新之间所做的事。在我这里的这个小动画里，如果你假设这个移动的圆是一个对象，而这是在客户端机器上运行的模拟

cues.en: and the green stars
cues.zh: 而那些绿色星星

cues.en: are updates coming in from the host about where this object really is and what direction it's really moving,
cues.zh: 是从主机传来的更新，说明这个对象真正在哪里、真正在往哪个方向移动，

cues.en: all the movement of the object in between the green stars and afterwards and predictably bouncing off walls and things like that,
cues.zh: 对象在绿色星星之间以及之后的所有移动，还有它可预测地撞墙反弹之类的情况，

cues.en: that's all prediction. That's all us applying rules and guesses about what we think is going to happen with the object.
cues.zh: 那全都是预测。那全都是我们应用规则和猜测，来判断我们认为这个对象接下来会发生什么。

cues.en: I'm going to throw this word around a little bit.
cues.zh: 我会稍微反复提到这个词。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: That was pretty painless. Now we're that much closer to looking at how we network beautiful things like this.
cues.zh: 这还挺轻松的。现在，我们离研究如何把这样漂亮的东西联网又近了一步。

cues.en: Networking stack.
cues.zh: 网络栈。

cues.en: If there's any old school network programmers in the room, you're probably expecting this to come up a little sooner,
cues.zh: 如果在座有老派的网络程序员，你们可能会觉得这个应该更早出现，

cues.en: but it doesn't look much like the OSI networking stack.
cues.zh: 但它看起来并不太像 OSI 网络栈。

cues.en: Let's run through it. The very highest level we have the game code, everything everyone else works on who's not on the networking team simply runs the game.
cues.zh: 我们来过一遍。最顶层是游戏代码，所有不属于网络团队、负责其他工作的人的代码，都会直接运行游戏。

cues.en: The next level below the game we call the game interface.
cues.zh: 游戏下面的一层，我们称之为游戏接口。

cues.en: The game interface is responsible for scraping the game, for extracting all the data from the game that we might potentially want to replicate.
cues.zh: 游戏接口负责抓取游戏，从游戏中提取所有我们可能想要复制的数据。

cues.en: The prioritization layer then takes all that data that game interface has gathered
cues.zh: 然后，优先级层会接收游戏接口收集的所有数据，

cues.en: and decides what stuff is most important to send.
cues.zh: 并决定哪些内容最重要，应该发送出去。

cues.en: Once the prioritization layer has selected what to send,
cues.zh: 优先级层选定要发送的内容后，

cues.en: we hand it off to the replication layer which implements essentially the tribe's protocols. Again, we're going to look at all this in more detail.
cues.zh: 我们会把它交给复制层，由它实现基本上属于 Tribe 的协议。我们稍后会更详细地介绍这些内容。

cues.en: Below that we have things we're not going to look at in detail. The channel manager which is flow and congestion control to keep us from flooding
cues.zh: 再往下是一些我们不会详细介绍的部分。其中，通道管理器负责流量控制和拥塞控制，避免我们把玩家的连接

cues.en: players connections
cues.zh: 淹没，

cues.en: and the transport layer which looks like everybody else's transport layer, just across platform socket layer.
cues.zh: 传输层则和其他系统的传输层类似，只不过位于跨平台套接字层之上。

cues.en: Okay. In this talk, we're going to cover these three layers specifically
cues.zh: 好。在这次演讲中，我们将专门讲这三个层

cues.en: in pretty good depth.
cues.zh: 而且会讲得相当深入。

cues.en: We're not going to talk about anything below or above.
cues.zh: 更底层或更上层的内容我们都不讲。

cues.en: Okay, some meat, some actual
cues.zh: 好，来点干货，一些真正的

cues.en: real algorithms instead of just overviews.
cues.zh: 真正的算法，而不只是概览。

cues.en: State data. This is the first tribes protocol and the one that accounts for the vast majority of our bandwidth.
cues.zh: 状态数据。这是三种协议中的第一种，也占用了我们绝大部分带宽。

cues.en: State data provides this very specific guarantee.
cues.zh: 状态数据提供了非常具体的保证。

cues.en: Eventually,
cues.zh: 最终，

cues.en: the most current state will arrive.
cues.zh: 最新的状态会到达。

cues.en: Sounds simple,
cues.zh: 听起来很简单，

cues.en: but it's incredibly powerful.
cues.zh: 但它非常强大。

cues.en: What does this mean? Let's say I was the host and my position on this stage was being replicated out to all of you as clients.
cues.zh: 这是什么意思？假设我是主机，我在这舞台上的位置会被复制给作为客户端的你们所有人。

cues.en: Say further, this position is being replicated as state data.
cues.zh: 进一步说，这个位置是作为状态数据来复制的。

cues.en: If I start in this position and you all know that I'm here, we start from time zero, everything is in sync and then I walk across the stage
cues.zh: 如果我从这个位置开始，你们都知道我在这里，我们从时间零点开始，一切同步，然后我走过舞台

cues.en: and then I stop.
cues.zh: 然后我停下。

cues.en: State data guarantees that if I stand here for long enough and the connection is not dropped,
cues.zh: 状态数据保证，如果我在这里站得够久，并且连接没有断开，

cues.en: you will all eventually see me appear at this location.
cues.zh: 你们最终都会看到我出现在这个位置。

cues.en: It does not guarantee any of the intermediate locations that will be sent.
cues.zh: 它不保证任何中间位置会被发送。

cues.en: All the intermediate information can be dropped based on available bandwidth.
cues.zh: 所有中间信息都可以根据可用带宽被丢弃。

cues.en: So this is used for all the vast majority of properties in our game, object positions, healths, timers, tons and tons of properties.
cues.zh: 所以它被用于我们游戏中的绝大多数属性：物体位置、生命值、计时器，以及大量大量属性。

cues.en: The second replication protocol
cues.zh: 第二种复制协议

cues.en: is called events.
cues.zh: 叫做事件。

cues.en: Events
cues.zh: 事件

cues.en: are all about justifying
cues.zh: 核心就是用更丰富的数据来佐证

cues.en: state data transitions with richer data.
cues.zh: 状态数据的转换。

cues.en: Events have much, much better screenshots than state data as you can see because events are all about telling you the thing about why something happened, why someone's health died or dropped, why someone died, why a warthog has just lost a wheel, all these sorts of things.
cues.zh: 比起状态数据，事件展示出的画面要精彩得多，大家也能看到，因为事件讲述的是事情发生的原因——为什么某人的生命值下降了、为什么有人阵亡了、为什么疣猪兽掉了个轮子，诸如此类。

cues.en: The event
cues.zh: 事件的

cues.en: reliability guarantee
cues.zh: 可靠性保证

cues.en: is non existent.
cues.zh: 是根本不存在的。

cues.en: Unlike state data which guarantees the eventual delivery of the most up to date state,
cues.zh: 状态数据会保证最终送达最新的状态，但与它不同的是，

cues.en: events have no guarantees whatsoever. Every event could potentially be dropped.
cues.zh: 事件没有任何保证。每个事件都有可能被丢弃。

cues.en: This is important because events are describing
cues.zh: 这一点很重要，因为事件描述的是

cues.en: transitions.
cues.zh: 状态转换过程。

cues.en: If you are not in a location where you can currently see the transition occurring, like if you are for example outside this room, you don't care about transitions that are occurring within this room, you only care about the final state. So if you were to enter the room you would see the updated state.
cues.zh: 如果你所在的位置看不到正在发生的过程，比如你在房间外面，你就不会关心房间内发生的过渡过程，你只关心最终状态。所以当你走进房间时，直接看到的就是更新后的状态。

cues.en: Last replication protocol, control data.
cues.zh: 最后一种同步协议：控制数据。

cues.en: Control data is all about improving the accuracy of our prediction systems.
cues.zh: 控制数据的核心就是提高预测系统的准确性。

cues.en: For control data, we take a
cues.zh: 对于控制数据，我们会采集

cues.en: sub sample of the player's controller inputs and a few other useful things And we transmit that sort of as frequently as we can
cues.zh: 玩家手柄输入的子采样以及其他一些有用信息，并尽可能频繁地

cues.en: from the client to the host and reflect it back out to all clients.
cues.zh: 从客户端发送给主机，再由主机广播给所有客户端。

cues.en: What this lets us do is it lets us infer changes in the game or predict changes in the game
cues.zh: 这样做的作用，是让我们能够推断或预测游戏中的变化，

cues.en: far in advance of when they would actually change the game. For example, if I'm running forward and then I push the left stick
cues.zh: 远早于这些变化真正在游戏中体现的时刻。例如，如果我正在向前跑，然后推左摇杆

cues.en: to start strafing left,
cues.zh: 开始向左平移，

cues.en: you won't actually see a change in my object for several frames plus acceleration time plus however long until it actually moves more than one pixel, you know, whatever, significant amount of time. Control data allows us to transmit the fact that I'm pushing my stick left
cues.zh: 在好几帧的时间里，再加上加速时间，以及直到真正移动超过一个像素所需的时长——总之是一段相当长的时间内——你其实根本看不到我的实体有任何变化。而控制数据允许我们把“我正在向左推摇杆”这一事实传输过去，

cues.en: so that everyone else can start to predict that I'm going to begin to strafe to improve the accuracy of their prediction.
cues.zh: 这样其他所有人就能提前预测我要开始侧移了，从而提高他们预测的准确度。

cues.en: This is a very, very tiny amount of data. Control data for one player is something like 20 bits.
cues.zh: 这是非常非常少的数据量。一个玩家的控制数据大约只有20比特。

cues.en: Very, very carefully hand packed data because it's sent so often.
cues.zh: 非常非常精心手工打包的数据，因为它发送得太频繁了。

cues.en: Okay. Let's look at the big picture putting together all these protocols in one.
cues.zh: 好。让我们看看全局，把所有协议整合到一起。

cues.en: We have a host box and a client box as all good networking diagrams should.
cues.zh: 我们有一个主机盒和一个客户端盒，这是所有好的网络图都应该有的。

cues.en: Firstly, the client sends control data to the host.
cues.zh: 首先，客户端向主机发送控制数据。

cues.en: This includes both his stick inputs and the current information about where he thinks he is in the world like MyBipet is currently in a certain location. This is how the client exerts most of his agency in the world.
cues.zh: 这包括他的摇杆输入以及当前他认为自己在世界中所处位置的信息，比如MyBipet当前在某个位置。这是客户端在世界中发挥大部分自主权的方式。

cues.en: Second, clients will transmit events to the host. These are transient things the client can do that he needs the host's permission to do or that he needs the host to execute. He needs the host to actually change the world in response to these things he's trying to do.
cues.zh: 其次，客户端会向主机发送事件。这些是客户端可以做的瞬时事情，他需要主机的许可才能做，或者需要主机来执行。他需要主机实际改变世界来响应他试图做的这些事情。

cues.en: From host to client, the picture is a little bit bigger.
cues.zh: 从主机到客户端，情况稍微复杂一些。

cues.en: We have control data which is stripped down to just the minimum at this point, just the controller inputs that are useful for prediction.
cues.zh: 我们有控制数据，此时已经精简到最低限度，只有对预测有用的控制器输入。

cues.en: We have state data, this is the vast majority of all our bandwidth. Again, This is transmitting all of the final states,
cues.zh: 我们有状态数据，这是我们绝大部分带宽。同样，这是传输所有最终状态，

cues.en: all of the current states of everything that is important over time.
cues.zh: 所有随时间变化的重要事物的当前状态。

cues.en: And we have events which are just like the client sends to the host, they are justifications for the state data transitions that occurred.
cues.zh: 还有事件，就像客户端发送给主机的一样，它们是所发生的状态数据转换的理由。

cues.en: So let's take an example.
cues.zh: 我们来看个例子。

cues.en: Right here we have in state data, the Warthog now has a broken windshield.
cues.zh: 在状态数据中，Warthog 现在的前挡风玻璃碎了。

cues.en: That's a piece of state data that's transmitted. Windshield state is now broken.
cues.zh: 这就是传输的一条状态数据：挡风玻璃状态现在是破损。

cues.en: If that was the only thing we transmitted and we didn't transmit,
cues.zh: 如果我们只传输了这个，而没有传输：

cues.en: this Warthog just took damage at this point,
cues.zh: “这辆 Warthog 刚刚在此处受到了伤害”，

cues.en: you would just see the windshield permute.
cues.zh: 那你只会看到挡风玻璃突然就变了。

cues.en: Maybe there would be some fake effects to cover it up but we wouldn't really know why the windshield got broken.
cues.zh: 也许会有一些假效果来掩盖一下，但我们并不知道挡风玻璃为什么会碎。

cues.en: If you have the event, you see beautiful sparks, you see all the appropriate transitions,
cues.zh: 如果有事件数据，你就能看到漂亮的火花，看到所有合理的过渡，

cues.en: you have special sound effects, all the beautiful
cues.zh: 听到特定的音效，以及所有那些精彩的

cues.en: flavor material that describes why the state data transition took place.
cues.zh: 修饰细节，来说明为什么会发生这种状态转换。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: Again, I beat this drum several times now, you're going to hear me beat it several more times. Replication is never fully reliable.
cues.zh: 我之前多次强调过这点，接下来你们还会听我反复提：状态同步绝不是完全可靠的。

cues.en: Unreliability
cues.zh: 不可靠性

cues.en: enables aggressive prioritization
cues.zh: 催生了激进的优先级排序，

cues.en: which lets us deal with the fact that we don't really have an object cap, which lets us deal with the fact that we have 200 synchronized objects or more in a 16 player game. I mean it peaks well over 2,000.
cues.zh: 这让我们能够应对没有真正对象上限的情况，让我们能够应对 16 人游戏中同步 200 个甚至更多对象的情况——峰值甚至远超 2000 个。

cues.en: So what can we do with prioritization?
cues.zh: 那么有了优先级排序，我们能做些什么呢？

cues.en: We can give the power
cues.zh: 我们可以放权

cues.en: to our flow control layer,
cues.zh: 给流控层，

cues.en: to the guy who is looking at the current connection status and figuring out whether it's safe to currently send data without causing
cues.zh: 让负责监控当前连接状态、判断当前发数据是否安全的人来决定，避免引起

cues.en: packet loss or a latency spike.
cues.zh: 丢包或延迟骤增。

cues.en: We can give this flow control layer that full authority. He decides when to send a packet. He decides when it's safe and how big it should be.
cues.zh: 我们可以把全部权限交给这个流控层。由它决定何时发包，由它决定何时安全以及包该有多大。

cues.en: When he decides to send a packet,
cues.zh: 当它决定发送一个数据包时，

cues.en: he talks to the replication layer and says hey we're sending a packet now, what would like write?
cues.zh: 它会和复制层通信，说：“嘿，我们现在要发送数据包了，你想写入什么？”

cues.en: Replication
cues.zh: Replication

cues.en: fills up the packet however big it is. Obviously we don't have room to fit all our data, we never do, we don't really have 20 megabit connections and even if we did, wouldn't have the perf to actually encode it all into a packet.
cues.zh: 会把数据包尽可能填满。显然，我们没有空间容纳所有数据；实际上从来都没有。我们并没有 20 Mbps 的连接，就算有，也没有足够的性能把所有内容编码进一个数据包。

cues.en: So we write high priority data first of course. We write data in priority order.
cues.zh: 所以，当然要先写入高优先级数据。我们会按照优先级顺序写入数据。

cues.en: Alright.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: We've sold our souls in terms of complexity to get this wonderful prioritization system, so let's take a quick look at what its capabilities are.
cues.zh: 为了实现这个出色的优先级系统，我们在复杂性上已经出卖了灵魂，所以快速看看它具备哪些能力。

cues.en: It's sort of what you would expect. It's
cues.zh: 它基本符合你的预期。它

cues.en: similar to the problem of culling, of like figuring out what stuff is important to render. It's a little bit of a softer problem.
cues.zh: 有点像裁剪问题，也就是判断哪些内容重要、需要渲染。这是一个稍微更宽松的问题。

cues.en: But basically we're looking at, hey, what stuff is close to this client?
cues.zh: 但基本上，我们会考虑：哪些东西离这个客户端比较近？

cues.en: What stuff is he looking at? What stuff could hurt him? What stuff has he recently damaged?
cues.zh: 他在看什么？哪些东西可能伤害他？哪些东西最近对他造成过伤害？

cues.en: Because that's a pretty strong indicator of interest.
cues.zh: 因为这通常是判断他是否感兴趣的强烈信号。

cues.en: There's some really unintuitive stuff you get in here which
cues.zh: 这里还有一些非常反直觉的内容，

cues.en: we have evolved over time.
cues.zh: 是我们随着时间逐步演变出来的。

cues.en: Things like, oh,
cues.zh: 比如说，

cues.en: grenades as they fly through the air are prioritized based on how likely they are to damage a particular player.
cues.zh: 手雷在空中飞行时，会根据它们伤害特定玩家的可能性进行优先级排序。

cues.en: That seemed reasonable to us. If it's not going to damage you, why do you care?
cues.zh: 这对我们来说似乎很合理。如果它不会伤害你，你为什么要在意它？

cues.en: But we discovered
cues.zh: 但我们发现

cues.en: significant lag artifact on the player's own grenades because players watch their own grenades like hawks even though they are completely irrelevant to them after they've thrown them, they can't affect them in any way. Well, that's not true. In general, they can't affect them in any way.
cues.zh: 玩家自己的手雷会出现明显的延迟伪影，因为玩家会像鹰一样盯着自己扔出的手雷，尽管手雷扔出去之后对他们完全无关紧要，也不可能再以任何方式影响他们。当然，这么说也不完全准确。一般来说，它们确实不可能以任何方式影响他们。

cues.en: You can shoot grenades out of the air, crazy sandbox designers.
cues.zh: 你能把空中的手榴弹打爆，疯狂的沙盒设计师。

cues.en: There's tons and tons of these special cases that we have sort of built up over the years
cues.zh: 多年来，我们积累了大量的这类特殊处理

cues.en: in response to player feedback to give the best behavior that we can.
cues.zh: 都是根据玩家反馈做出的，目的是尽可能提供最佳行为表现。

cues.en: Let's look at a quick example of this. This is a screenshot taken from a Halo Reach game.
cues.zh: 来看一个简单的例子。这是《光环：致远星》游戏里的一张截图。

cues.en: This player here in the lower left has just killed the player who is now ragdolling and falling to the ground below him.
cues.zh: 左下角这名玩家刚刚击杀了另一名玩家，对方现在正变成布娃娃物理状态，往下掉落。

cues.en: Let's take a look at the network prioritization
cues.zh: 我们来看看网络优先级是怎么处理的

cues.en: of data about these objects to the guy who's still alive. So everything we're going to see is about sending data to the guy who's still alive.

cues.en: Four rules for designing your gameplay networking systems.
cues.zh: 设计游戏玩法网络系统的四条规则。

cues.en: First,
cues.zh: 第一，

cues.en: you have to decide for each gameplay mechanic and sort of some high level principles as well which parts of your game are adjudicated by a single authority
cues.zh: 你必须为每个玩法机制、以及一些高层原则做出决定：游戏的哪些部分由单一权威来裁决，

cues.en: versus the parts that are allowed to be predicted and allowed to be out of sync for brief periods?
cues.zh: 哪些部分允许被预测、允许短暂地不同步？

cues.en: The more stuff is adjudicated by the authority, the fairer and more consistent the game is.
cues.zh: 由权威裁决的部分越多，游戏就越公平、越一致。

cues.en: The more stuff that's predicted,
cues.zh: 预测的内容越多，

cues.en: the more responsive the game is.
cues.zh: 游戏的响应就越灵敏。

cues.en: Most often you will have to mix
cues.zh: 大多数情况下，你甚至必须

cues.en: these paradigms even within every individual game mechanic.
cues.zh: 在单个游戏机制内混合使用这些范式。

cues.en: As we saw, you have to split the mechanic up and make predicted the pretty pieces and make adjudicated the important pieces.
cues.zh: 正如我们看到的，你必须拆分机制，让好看的部分做预测，让关键的部分做裁决。

cues.en: Second, always, always
cues.zh: 第二，永远，永远都要

cues.en: ask where you're hiding the lag.
cues.zh: 搞清楚你把延迟藏在哪了。

cues.en: You can save yourself from shipping ugly public beta networking like we did.
cues.zh: 这样你就能避免像我们当年一样，公测时端出糟糕的网络体验。

cues.en: If you have host adjudication occurring,
cues.zh: 只要存在主机裁决，

cues.en: you will have lag somewhere.
cues.zh: 某些地方就必然会有延迟。

cues.en: If you don't have lag somewhere,
cues.zh: 如果看似哪里都没有延迟，

cues.en: you don't have host adjudication, you have incurred lag debt.
cues.zh: 那你就根本没做主机裁决，而是欠下了延迟债。

cues.en: Third,
cues.zh: 第三，

cues.en: don't be afraid to change game mechanics to improve networking.
cues.zh: 不要害怕为了改善网络而修改游戏机制。

cues.en: This is incredibly
cues.zh: 这点极其

cues.en: important. We have in the past several times had gameplay mechanics that we liked internally, that the design was very happy with and that played very well on LAN games.

cues.en: Halo three's shipping melee is a classic example.
cues.zh: Halo 3 首发时的近战机制就是一个经典例子。

cues.en: Was a fairly complex,
cues.zh: 那是一个相当复杂、

cues.en: well somewhat complex thing where when two players melee at each other at the same time, the player with more health would win.

cues.en: The other one would die. They felt this added tactical depth to the game.
cues.zh: 另一方则会阵亡。策划觉得这增加了游戏的战术深度。

cues.en: In practice on the internet with a few hundred milliseconds of latency,
cues.zh: 但在实际公网环境下，面对几百毫秒的延迟，

cues.en: you couldn't

cues.zh: 这意味着它拥有大量的内部防护和故障转移机制。

cues.en: Which means that if you have some system that is horribly broken somewhere in your networking tree,
cues.zh: 这意味着，如果你的网络结构某处有严重故障，

cues.en: you probably won't notice it for a very long time because one of the safeguards
cues.zh: 你可能很久都不会发现，因为某个保护机制

cues.en: will save you
cues.zh: 会帮你兜住

cues.en: while consuming a ton of extra bandwidth or being inefficient in some other way.
cues.zh: 但同时会消耗大量额外带宽，或者在其他方面效率低下。

cues.en: At the end of Halo three and when Halo three shipped, we had built up a couple games worth this sort of entropy
cues.zh: 在《光环3》开发末期和发售时，我们已经积累了好几个游戏份量的这种熵

cues.en: and as a result 16 player games in Halo three did not work very consistently. There were a great percentage of lag artifacts. And so this richest,
cues.zh: 结果《光环3》的16人游戏运行得很不稳定。出现了很大比例的延迟卡顿。于是这个最丰富、

cues.en: most complex, most chaotic version of Halo which we all loved so much didn't really work very well on the Internet and we were sad.
cues.zh: 最复杂、最混乱的《光环》版本，我们都很喜欢，却在互联网上表现不太好，我们很难过。

cues.en: So we said, hey, let's go in, let's attack it, let's optimize it.
cues.zh: 于是我们说，嘿，动手吧，攻克它，优化它。

cues.en: Optimization is super dangerous.
cues.zh: 优化超级危险。

cues.en: It's really easy using your expert knowledge of the system and your belief that you yourself are a smart person, which we all share I'm sure,
cues.zh: 很容易利用你对系统的专家知识，以及你相信自己是个聪明人——我们肯定都这么想——

cues.en: to think about
cues.zh: 去思考

cues.en: the architecture of your networking.
cues.zh: 你的网络架构。

cues.en: Decide something that seems like it could be better,
cues.zh: 决定某个看起来可能更好的方案，

cues.en: implement an optimization, gain some small amount of efficiency
cues.zh: 实施一项优化，获得一点点效率提升

cues.en: and introduce a ton of bugs.
cues.zh: 却引入一大堆 bug。

cues.en: Again, this all comes back to test coverage. You can't really fully test your networking It's incredibly, incredibly hard and requires just vast, vast resources.
cues.zh: 这又回到测试覆盖率。你没法真正完整测试你的网络，这极其极其困难，需要海量资源。

cues.en: So changing architecture
cues.zh: 所以改变架构

cues.en: is something that has to be done very, very deliberately.
cues.zh: 是必须非常非常刻意去做的事。

cues.en: What this means is the kinds of optimizations you will think of from thinking about how your architecture currently works will usually not be the best bang for the buck.
cues.zh: 这意味着，单纯从现有架构去琢磨出来的优化方案，往往性价比不是最高的。

cues.en: Really, we don't want to be optimizing without good data. We don't want to just be going in and thinking about functions that are slow on a CPU optimizing or events we think are big on network optimizing and go in and change them. What we want is data.
cues.zh: 实际上，没有可靠的数据，我们绝不该盲目优化。不能光凭感觉觉得某个函数耗 CPU 就去改，或者觉得哪个网络事件开销大就去优化。我们要的是数据。

cues.en: This is one of my favorite quotes
cues.zh: 这是我最喜欢的一句名言，

cues.en: from the other Michael Jackson.
cues.zh: 出自“另一个”Michael Jackson。

cues.en: First rule of program optimization,
cues.zh: 程序优化的第一法则：

cues.en: don't do it. Second rule for experts only,
cues.zh: 不要优化。第二法则，仅供专家参考：

cues.en: don't do it yet.
cues.zh: 先别优化。

cues.en: Well we knew we needed to do it unfortunately. We couldn't follow Mr. Jackson's advice. So inspection tools are what you need to get past this problem, to get to where it's okay to optimize.
cues.zh: 但不幸的是，我们明知不得不做，无法遵循 Jackson 先生的建议。所以你需要借助检查工具来跨过这道坎，达到真正可以开始优化的阶段。

cues.en: Deep inspection tools will help you identify the things that are the best bang for the buck.
cues.zh: 深度检查工具能帮你找出性价比最高的优化点。

cues.en: So we thought about this. We sort of figured this out. We said okay, need some tools. What do we need? Well, let's think about how we do CPU optimization like
cues.zh: 所以我们仔细琢磨，理清了思路，觉得需要一些工具。那到底需要什么？不妨想想我们平时是怎么做 CPU 优化的：

cues.en: we boot up the game and we run some representative test case and then we gather data which gives us a nice hierarchical view
cues.zh: 启动游戏，跑一些典型的测试用例，然后收集数据，得到一个清晰的层级视图，

cues.en: of where all of our time is going and then we figure out the best bang for the buck pieces and optimize them.
cues.zh: 看清时间到底都花在哪儿了，再找出性价比最高的部分去优化。

cues.en: So we built some profilers. That seemed natural.
cues.zh: 于是我们顺理成章地构建了一些性能分析工具。

cues.en: They would track bandwidth use for us and priority calculation results and show them on screen.
cues.zh: 它们能帮我们追踪带宽占用以及优先级计算结果，并把这些信息实时显示在屏幕上。

cues.en: Let's take a look at some of the capabilities of our profilers that we built.
cues.zh: 我们来看看我们构建的分析器有哪些功能。

cues.en: So this is from a live game of Reach, this video recording
cues.zh: 所以这段录像来自一场 Reach 的实况比赛

cues.en: and we bring up this graph view. A bunch of configuration stuff at the top,
cues.zh: 然后我们打开这个图表视图。顶部是一堆配置项，

cues.en: data series in center and then graphing of the data series at the bottom. You can't read these numbers or you can see a lot of these lines, don't worry about it, not important.
cues.zh: 数据序列在中间，然后在底部绘制该数据序列的图表。你可能看不清这些数字，或者会看到很多这样的线，别担心，这不重要。

cues.en: What's important is the kind of content being presented here. The first line here is showing
cues.zh: 重要的是这里呈现的内容类型。这里的第一行展示的是

cues.en: the entirety of replication
cues.zh: 复制的全部内容

cues.en: used bandwidth.
cues.zh: 已用带宽。

cues.en: The total amount of data being sent. Now it's split into five lines. This is showing all of our replication bandwidth use by protocol type. So state data as one, events as another, control data
cues.zh: 这是正在发送的数据总量。现在它被拆分成了五条线，按协议类型展示了我们所有的复制带宽使用情况。比如状态数据是一类，事件是一类，控制数据……

cues.en: and then voice.
cues.zh: 然后是语音。

cues.en: In particular you can see here, well if take
cues.zh: 特别是，你可以在这里看到，嗯，如果我们取……

cues.en: a look at the GDC vault and look at the good version of the video, can see that state data takes up about 80% of our bandwidth.
cues.zh: 看看 GDC Vault 和视频的清晰版，就能看到状态数据大约占了我们 80% 的带宽。

cues.en: Hey, there's a lot more lines now. We've just gone another level deeper.
cues.zh: 嘿，现在多出好多行。我们又深入了一层。

cues.en: We can go inside state data and events and look at individual types of events and individual classes of objects.
cues.zh: 我们可以深入状态数据和事件，查看各个事件类型和各个对象类别。

cues.en: So we can look at
cues.zh: 所以我们可以看看

cues.en: bipeds versus
cues.zh: 双足动物 vs

cues.en: weapons versus items and look at all their bandwidth use.
cues.zh: 对比武器和道具，并查看它们全部的带宽占用情况。

cues.en: We can go even one level deeper which is shown here. We can look at every individual property
cues.zh: 我们可以再深入一层，如图所示。我们可以查看每一个单独的属性。

cues.en: of every subtype of every type of replication. So we can look at biped positions and compare them to weapon inventories.
cues.zh: 每种复制类型的每个子类型。这样我们就能查看双足角色的位置，并把它们和武器库存作比较。

cues.en: All of this data is shown of course with a nice graphing view so you can see which types are spiky. Very, very important in any kind of optimization.
cues.zh: 所有这些数据当然都会用漂亮的图表视图展示出来，让你看到哪些类型出现尖峰。这在任何优化里都非常非常重要。

cues.en: Now this is all very useful. This gives us a nice like sort of a high level classification based view of bandwidth use but one other really interesting thing especially in combination with priority information is per object bandwidth use which I just turned on in the background. There's a sea of numbers there.
cues.zh: 这些都很有用。它给了我们一个基于高层分类的带宽使用视图，但另一个很有意思的东西，尤其结合优先级信息时，是按对象的带宽使用，我刚在后台打开了。那里全是数字。

cues.en: Our profiler tracks for every individual object all of the bandwidth use associated with that object
cues.zh: 我们的分析器会跟踪每个单独对象所有与之相关的带宽使用

cues.en: as well as all of the bandwidth that the object would like to use in an ideal world. And it tracks all those and shows them here and they're color coded by who's using the most bandwidth versus the least.
cues.zh: 以及该对象在理想情况下希望使用的所有带宽。它会跟踪所有这些并显示在这里，并按谁使用带宽最多到最少进行颜色编码。

cues.en: And this can let us identify things like
cues.zh: 这可以让我们识别出像

cues.en: individual objects that are sitting off in a corner and chewing up bandwidth for no apparent reason which happens all the time.
cues.zh: 那些缩在角落里、毫无明显理由地消耗带宽的单独对象，而这种事经常发生。

cues.en: So that's our profiling tool. We built this in, I don't know, about a month, maybe three weeks
cues.zh: 这就是我们的性能分析工具。我们大概用了一个月，我不知道，也许三周，把它做了出来

cues.en: and we decided to go and attack,
cues.zh: 然后我们决定着手解决，

cues.en: I'm getting ahead of myself. We had one other tool besides profilers to work with.
cues.zh: 我有点讲快了。除了分析器，我们还有一个工具可以用。

cues.en: This tool is called films. Films are something we've had since Halo three.
cues.zh: 这个工具叫 Films。Films 是我们从《光环3》就有的东西。

cues.en: They provide us with deterministic playback of gameplay sessions. They're called films instead of deterministic playback of gameplay sessions because they're a user facing feature. Players can actually record their gameplay sessions
cues.zh: 它们为我们提供游戏过程的确定性回放。它们叫 Films 而不是“游戏过程的确定性回放”，因为它们是面向用户的功能。玩家实际上可以录制自己的游戏过程

cues.en: and play them back.
cues.zh: 并回放它们。

cues.en: These are very, very useful for debugging gameplay
cues.zh: 这些对调试游戏玩法非常非常有用

cues.en: but they've never been really very useful for network debugging
cues.zh: 但对网络调试从来都不太有用

cues.en: because network systems are of course idle during film playback. Networking is all about live decisions. It's all about looking at the current state of the internet and making decisions.
cues.zh: 因为网络系统在影片回放期间当然是空闲的。网络全靠实时决策，全靠观察互联网的当前状态并做出决策。

cues.en: So that was sort of neat. So we looked at these and we said, hey, we've got this profiler on the one hand, seems pretty sweet. We've got these films on the other hand that everyone loves, all the gameplay guys sort of thumb their noses at us with their incredibly easy to repro bugs.
cues.zh: 所以这还挺巧妙的。我们看了这些之后说，嘿，一边有性能分析器，看起来挺不错；另一边有大家都喜欢的影片，而玩法组的同事凭着他们那些极易复现的 bug 对我们嗤之以鼻。

cues.en: And we said, hey, these things sure would taste good together.
cues.zh: 我们说，嘿，这两样东西搭配起来肯定很不错。

cues.en: Can we make that happen?
cues.zh: 能实现吗？

cues.en: And of course we're engineers, we can.
cues.zh: 当然，我们是工程师，当然能。

cues.en: So we spliced
cues.zh: 于是我们把

cues.en: the network profiler data into the film at the times when gameplay was occurring. So after every frame of gameplay we would inject a little debug blob into our films that are being streamed out to the console hard drive
cues.zh: 网络分析器的数据拼接进影片中发生游戏玩法的时刻。所以每帧玩法之后，我们会往流式写入主机硬盘的影片里注入一小块调试数据

cues.en: containing all of the new network state that was sampled during that frame. So all the information about every packet we sent and received and all the prioritization decisions.
cues.zh: 其中包含该帧期间采样的所有新网络状态。也就是我们收发的每个数据包以及所有优先级决策的全部信息。

cues.en: For the first time in Halo history, we could analyze network performance after the fact
cues.zh: 在 Halo 历史上，我们第一次能在事后分析网络性能

cues.en: which just enabled all kinds of wonderful
cues.zh: 这开启了一系列奇妙的

cues.en: deep investigations we've never been able to do before.
cues.zh: 深入调查，这是我们以前从未能做到的。

cues.en: Alright.
cues.zh: 好了。

cues.en: Profilers and films are all very well, but we still need some way to actually gather data to actually
cues.zh: 性能分析器和回放录像都很好，但我们仍需要某种方法来真正收集数据，真正……

cues.en: figure out whether the game is working well. So we need to playtest. We need to play the game. That's the ultimate test.
cues.zh: 弄清楚游戏运行状况是否良好。所以我们需要做游戏测试。我们需要亲自玩这款游戏，这才是终极检验。

cues.en: So we ran network per focus playtest about once a month.
cues.zh: 于是我们大约每个月组织一次专门针对网络的游戏测试。

cues.en: We ran network filters on all the boxes in the lab so that we could simulate all kinds of different network conditions, packet loss, limited bandwidth,
cues.zh: 我们在实验室的所有机器上运行网络过滤器，以此模拟各种不同的网络环境：丢包、带宽受限、

cues.en: latency spikes, brief connection drops,
cues.zh: 延迟突增、短暂掉线，

cues.en: all sorts of things like that.
cues.zh: 诸如此类的各种状况。

cues.en: And then we had players play.
cues.zh: 然后我们让玩家进行游戏。

cues.en: And then we ran up into a problem very quickly.
cues.zh: 接着我们很快就遇到了一个问题。

cues.en: Players can play and they can sort of tell us whether they had a good time or not,
cues.zh: 玩家可以玩，也能大致告诉我们他们玩得开不开心，

cues.en: whether they thought the networking was laggy or not,
cues.zh: 觉得网络到底卡不卡，

cues.en: which incidentally correlates almost perfectly with whether they won or not.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，这往往跟他们到底赢没赢几乎完全正相关。

cues.en: But really this wasn't very scientific and it wasn't very granular. It wasn't helping us figure out whether we were actually making our networking better.
cues.zh: 但说实在的，这不够科学，粒度也太粗，根本帮不了我们弄清楚网络质量到底有没有改善。

cues.en: We needed a more scientific way to measure success.
cues.zh: 我们需要一种更科学的方式来衡量成果。

cues.en: So what do we do? We allow players to report every time they see lag
cues.zh: 那我们是怎么做的呢？我们让玩家每次感觉卡顿就进行上报，

cues.en: by pushing a controller button especially assigned for that purpose in these playtests.
cues.zh: 具体做法就是在测试中按下一个专门为此分配的手柄按键。

cues.en: This injects an additional debug blob into the wonderful film
cues.zh: 这会在录像数据中注入一个额外的调试数据块，

cues.en: allowing us to jump to it later and look at what they saw and investigate why they saw lag.
cues.zh: 方便我们后续直接跳转过去，查看他们当时的画面，并排查导致卡顿的原因。

cues.en: This is how we turned this from an art,
cues.zh: 我们就是通过这种方式，把它从一门玄学、

cues.en: a guessing based game and an incredibly labor intensive game into a science.
cues.zh: 一种全凭猜测且极度耗费人力的差事，转变成了一门真正的科学。

cues.en: When we could run the game at our bandwidth goals and get no perceived lag events coming out of the players,
cues.zh: 当游戏能在我们的带宽目标下运行，而且玩家不再反馈任何感知延迟时，

cues.en: we knew we had succeeded.
cues.zh: 我们就知道自己成功了。

cues.en: There were a few bumps along the way.
cues.zh: 一路上也遇到过一些坎坷。

cues.en: Most notably, as we went through our network optimizations,
cues.zh: 最明显的是，在我们进行网络优化期间，

cues.en: we started discovering that perceived lag events were still getting put in by players. They were still pushing the button.
cues.zh: 我们发现玩家依然在上报感知延迟事件。他们还在按那个反馈按钮。

cues.en: We didn't really understand it. We would go in and we would look at the films and look at what they saw and they didn't see any lag. There was no network lag. Was plenty of bandwidth available.
cues.zh: 我们当时百思不得其解。我们去调看录像，查看他们看到的画面，但根本没有任何卡顿。完全没有网络延迟，带宽也十分充裕。

cues.en: Instead they would push this button whenever some game mechanic
cues.zh: 相反，每当某种游戏机制

cues.en: confused them.
cues.zh: 让他们感到困惑时，他们就会去按这个按钮。

cues.en: If they got shot from behind by two guys at once and the death camera didn't show them how they got killed clearly enough, they would hit the button and be like that looked laggy.
cues.zh: 比如他们同时被背后两个人射杀，而死亡镜头又没交代清楚死因，他们就会按按钮，觉得“刚才好像卡了”。

cues.en: It got incredibly subtle things like the, at one point we had, we were tuning grenade damage in the Alpha and grenades were tuned up somewhat from their Halo three level so a grenade could kill you in one shot much more often than at a larger distance.
cues.zh: 情况甚至会微妙到这种程度：有一次在 Alpha 测试中调整手雷伤害，手雷威力比 Halo 3 调高了一些，更容易在更远距离一击秒杀。

cues.en: And in pre Alpha network
cues.zh: 而在 Pre-Alpha 阶段的网络

cues.en: perf tests,
cues.zh: 性能测试中，

cues.en: we got a significant number of perceived lag events inserted when players would get killed by these grenades because getting killed in one shot from nearly full health is very confusing and feels very disorienting.
cues.zh: 大量玩家被手雷击杀后提交了感知延迟事件，因为接近满血被一击秒杀让人非常费解，也会让人完全摸不着头脑。

cues.en: So we would bring these things to our designers and send them these little sub snippets of films and say hey, these game mechanics are confusing players, they think they're laggy. And we had science to back it up.
cues.zh: 所以，我们会把这些内容拿给设计师看，再把这些电影片段的小片段发给他们，说：“你看，这些游戏机制让玩家感到困惑，他们以为是卡顿。”而且我们有科学依据来支持这一点。

cues.en: Alright, the culmination of all of this.
cues.zh: 好了，这就是这一切的成果。

cues.en: I'm going to show you the same section of gameplay that we looked at before.
cues.zh: 我要向你们展示之前看过的同一段游戏画面。

cues.en: I'm going to talk about everything working together.
cues.zh: 我要讲讲这一切是如何协同工作的。

cues.en: So this is not a live game. This is not a video of a live game. This is a video of one of our films playing back.
cues.zh: 所以，这不是一个正在运行的游戏，也不是一段正在运行的游戏视频，而是我们某部影片回放的视频。

cues.en: So we can go into third person and view the game from different perspectives.
cues.zh: 我们可以切换到第三人称视角，从不同角度查看游戏。

cues.en: We can fly the camera around and view what's happening in the game to our heart's content.
cues.zh: 我们可以随意移动摄像机，尽情查看游戏中发生的一切。

cues.en: Even more powerfully,
cues.zh: 更强大的是，

cues.en: we can rewind.
cues.zh: 我们可以倒带。

cues.en: We can go back and we can view a questionable section of the game over and over with these powerful profiling tools available to us.
cues.zh: 我们可以回到之前，借助这些强大的性能分析工具，反复查看游戏中可疑的片段。

cues.en: There is no excuse to us for not tracking down
cues.zh: 有了这套工具，

cues.en: lag problems given this tool set.
cues.zh: 我们没有理由不找出卡顿问题的根源。

cues.en: Of course it gets even more interesting.
cues.zh: 当然，事情还会变得更有意思。

cues.en: All of the stuff I've shown you up until now is all of the network data of the host box in one big bucket. Like the graph is showing all the bandwidth use of the host to all clients. That's not really the most interesting thing. The most interesting thing is this, which looks sort of the same to you but you have to take my word for it.
cues.zh: 到目前为止，我展示的所有内容，都是主机的全部网络数据，混在一个大桶里。也就是说，图表显示的是主机向所有客户端使用的全部带宽。但这其实不是最有意思的部分。最有意思的是这个，它看起来和刚才差不多，但你得相信我的话。

cues.en: This is showing bandwidth as sent to the particular client there with the sword only.
cues.zh: 这里显示的只是发送给那个手持剑的特定客户端的带宽。

cues.en: This is the contents of the packets that we sent to him in this game at this time.
cues.zh: 这是此时我们在游戏中发送给他的数据包内容。

cues.en: We can also go in and look at a particular object like this shotgun
cues.zh: 我们也可以进去查看某个特定对象，比如这把霰弹枪，

cues.en: and press a button and filter all of our data being sent to that one guy
cues.zh: 按个按钮，筛选出发给那个家伙的所有数据，

cues.en: with the sword to show only data sent about that shotgun. Similarly this biped.
cues.zh: 也就是拿着剑的那个家伙，只显示关于那把霰弹枪发送的数据。这个双足角色同理。

cues.en: We can say, oh, this is all the stuff we transmitted about that biped. This is the total output of our prioritization systems, the movement of that guy recently,
cues.zh: 我们可以说，哦，这就是我们传输的关于那个双足角色的全部内容。这是我们优先级系统的总输出，那个家伙最近的移动，

cues.en: every attribute we care about.
cues.zh: 我们关心的每个属性。

cues.en: But these are still one second averages. Oh, we can get way more detail than that. We have all the data. We can show every single packet that we sent to this client
cues.zh: 但这些仍然是一秒平均值。哦，我们还能看到远比这更多的细节。我们有全部数据。我们可以显示发给这个客户端的每一个数据包，

cues.en: and look inside them in this very visual way
cues.zh: 并以这种非常直观的方式查看内部，

cues.en: to see exactly which packets included updates about this guy,
cues.zh: 准确看出哪些数据包包含关于这个家伙的更新，

cues.en: what properties they included.
cues.zh: 它们包含哪些属性。

cues.en: We can scroll through time. We can scrub back and forth exactly like we could before.
cues.zh: 我们可以沿时间滚动。可以像之前一样来回拖动查看。

cues.en: This whole picture
cues.zh: 这整个图景

cues.en: is what allowed us to reduce the overall bandwidth use of Halo three pardon me, Halo Reach from Halo three
cues.zh: 正是它让我们把 Halo 3——抱歉，是 Halo Reach 相比 Halo 3——的整体带宽占用降低

cues.en: by over 80%.
The total time for development of these tools,
cues.zh: 开发这些工具的总时间，

cues.en: the film integration and the various visualizers,
cues.zh: 包括影片集成和各种可视化工具，

cues.en: somewhere on the order of six weeks
cues.zh: 大约六周左右，

cues.en: plus significant amount of time ongoing reviewing perceived lag events after playtests.
cues.zh: 再加上大量持续投入的时间，用于在试玩后复查感知到的延迟事件。

cues.en: Alright. So we took this wonderful process, taking you back in time again. We're at the end of Halo three. We're starting upper reach. We built this beautiful tool set. We integrated it into our films. We unleashed it on Halo three on internal builds. We said let's see what we find. I wonder what the problem is.
cues.zh: 好。所以我们采用了这个很棒的流程，再带你回到过去。我们处在 Halo 3 末期，正开始做 Halo Reach。我们构建了这套漂亮的工具集，把它集成进我们的影片流程，并在内部版本中对 Halo 3 全面使用。我们说看看能发现什么。我想知道问题到底是什么。

cues.en: And we got this wonderful high level breakdown of data and this is the first thing we harvested. This was even before we had network perf playtests.
cues.zh: 我们得到了一个非常棒的数据高层分析结果，这是我们采集到的第一批数据。当时我们甚至还没进行网络性能试玩。

cues.en: And we got okay, 50% of our data's positions, velocities and orientations, 20% player control, so forth.
cues.zh: 结果显示，大约 50% 的数据是玩家的位置、速度和朝向，20% 是玩家控制数据，其他数据依此类推。

cues.en: We said hey, let's go optimize the heavy hitters just like we would in CPU perf.
cues.zh: 我们想，既然这样，那就像做 CPU 性能优化一样，先优化这些占用最多的部分。

cues.en: This was a false start unfortunately.
cues.zh: 但遗憾的是，这是一次无效的尝试。

cues.en: Turns out
cues.zh: 结果发现，

cues.en: it's very, very difficult to further optimize positions, velocities and orientations. This is very much like seeing your math functions in your CPU profiles.
cues.zh: 要进一步优化位置、速度和朝向非常非常困难。这就像在 CPU 性能分析中看到数学函数一样。

cues.en: They are things that have to be done a lot. They're in a lot of algorithms.
cues.zh: 这些操作必须频繁执行，而且会出现在大量算法中。

cues.en: They tend to be already fairly optimal because everyone working on them knows they're going be used a lot.
cues.zh: 它们通常已经相当优化了，因为所有负责这些代码的人都知道它们会被大量使用。

cues.en: And so they, we didn't get much out of it. They were already pretty optimal from even their original implementations. So we need to go up to a higher level.
cues.zh: 所以，我们没从中得到多少收益。它们从最初实现开始就已经相当优化了。因此，我们需要提升到更高的层次。

cues.en: Here's some good optimizations.
cues.zh: 下面是一些有效的优化方法。

cues.en: First,
cues.zh: 首先，

cues.en: reducing always on bandwidth use. This was sort of a traditional networking optimization we would call it. We removed data that was duplicated,
cues.zh: 减少始终启用的带宽占用。这算是一种传统的网络优化。我们移除了重复的数据，

cues.en: sorry, so the control replication from hosts to clients
cues.zh: 抱歉，也就是说，从主机向客户端进行的控制状态复制

cues.en: accounted for a significant amount of upstream. We looked into it and we found that it didn't contain positions and orientations and velocities, it contained things we could compress pretty well.
cues.zh: 占用了相当多的上行带宽。我们深入分析后发现，其中并不包含位置、朝向和速度，而是包含了一些非常容易压缩的数据。

cues.en: So we went in and we removed a bunch of data that was duplicated, we removed data we could infer in other ways and we optimized some encoding by hand very carefully.
cues.zh: 于是我们着手去重了大量数据，去掉了能通过其他方式推断出的数据，还非常仔细地手动优化了一些编码。

cues.en: And we got this down about 60% by doing this just because we knew we had data, we knew it was a significant amount of bandwidth, we knew it was worth spending this time. So we spent like two weeks on this tiny section of code trying to just hand tweak the hell out of it.
cues.zh: 这样一来我们把数据量削减了大约 60%，因为我们清楚手头有数据，知道这占用了大量带宽，也明白花这个时间是值得的。所以我们花了大概两周，在这小段代码上拼了命地手动微调。

cues.en: And this worked out.
cues.zh: 结果很成功。

cues.en: This is the only optimization we implemented that I would consider a success that was actually a networking optimization.
cues.zh: 这是我们做过的所有优化里，我认为唯一算得上成功的、真正的网络优化。

cues.en: But yet I have many more slides.
cues.zh: 不过我后面还有好多页幻灯片呢。

cues.en: Let's take a look. Fixing a prioritization bug. So
cues.zh: 来看看这个：修复一个优先级 bug。事情是这样的，

cues.en: when guys die in Halo, they drop all this crap.
cues.zh: 在 Halo 里角色阵亡时，会掉落一大堆杂七杂八的东西。

cues.en: Two couple guns, couple grenades, that sort of thing. These fall to the ground and are simulated by havoc.
cues.zh: 两三把枪、几颗手雷之类的。它们掉在地上，由 Havok 进行物理模拟。

cues.en: We discovered a problem with the profiler.
cues.zh: 我们在 profiler 里发现了一个问题。

cues.en: Idle grenades
cues.zh: 闲置的手雷

cues.en: rolling around on the ground
cues.zh: 在地上滚来滚去，

cues.en: had incredibly high network priority. It just showed up to us like they're using all this bandwidth so they're red on object bandwidth display, bring up the priority profiler, there's a ton of data there, a ton of very,
cues.zh: 网络优先级居然高得离谱。它表现为占用了巨额带宽，在对象带宽显示里直接标红；打开优先级 profiler，里面赫然全是极高、

cues.en: very high priority numbers showing up.
cues.zh: 极高的优先级数值。

cues.en: And we said what on earth is going on? So we traced it back and we walked through the prioritization algorithms and we discovered that a bug fix was implemented at the end of Halo three which was causing this to happen.
cues.zh: 我们当时就纳闷这到底是怎么回事？于是顺藤摸瓜排查了优先级算法，发现原来是 Halo 3 研发末期合入的一个 bug 修复引发了这个问题。

cues.en: And so we traced back, why was this done? Like this is crazy. Why do idle grenades have such high priority?
cues.zh: 于是我们回溯追查，为什么会这么做？这太离谱了。为什么静止的手雷会有这么高的优先级？

cues.en: Turned out that at the end of Halo three,
cues.zh: 结果发现在 Halo 3 开发后期，

cues.en: about two weeks before RC,
cues.zh: 大概在 RC 前两周，

cues.en: equipment was given a huge priority boost. Equipment in Halo three was like these throwable things that could spawn bubble shields or drain people shields.
cues.zh: 装备获得了极大的优先级提升。Halo 3 里的装备就像那些能生成泡泡护盾或抽干别人护盾的投掷物。

cues.en: And equipment was laggy and so they gave it a big priority boost and they said, alright, we're, you know, that's all that. They tested it, it worked.
cues.zh: 当时装备同步很卡，所以他们大幅提升了它的优先级，心想，行了，搞定了。测试之后，确实奏效了。

cues.en: Turned out through an accident of design on the gameplay coder side,
cues.zh: 结果由于玩法程序员在设计上的一个意外巧合，

cues.en: grenades and equipment had the same parent class
cues.zh: 手雷和装备拥有相同的父类，

cues.en: which was called equipment.
cues.zh: 名字就叫 equipment。

cues.en: So all of the idle grenades on the ground without their pins pulled totally unthreatening to anyone received this same priority boost
cues.zh: 于是地上所有没拔掉引信、对谁都没有威胁的静止手雷，也都获得了同样的优先级提升，

cues.en: consuming tremendous amounts of bandwidth as they rolled around gently on the ground and waited for someone to pick them up.
cues.zh: 在地上轻轻滚动、等待被人捡起的同时，消耗了海量的带宽。

cues.en: Simple fix, one line, apply priority boost only to active equipment.
cues.zh: 修复很简单，就一行代码：只对处于激活状态的装备提升优先级。

cues.en: This by itself freed up probably 20% of our bandwidth.
cues.zh: 光是这一项，大概就帮我们释放了 20% 的带宽。

cues.en: The whole battle was identifying the issue.
cues.zh: 最艰难的部分全在于定位问题。

cues.en: Alright. Another example, a little different. Changing game mechanics. Halo three used a constant artificial friction on items, these idle grenades and weapons on the ground.
cues.zh: 好，另一个稍微有点不同的例子：修改游戏机制。Halo 3 对物品（也就是地上那些静止的手雷和武器）应用了恒定的人工阻力。

cues.en: As they rolled around on the ground,
cues.zh: 当它们在地上滚动时，

cues.en: applied this artificial friction to them to keep them from all rolling indefinitely until they reached the lowest point in the level.
cues.zh: 对其施加这种人工阻力，是为了防止它们无休止地滚动，直到掉到关卡的最低处。

cues.en: The problem with this was if you had an object on a hill, a relatively steep hill, the artificial friction would combat gravity and keep the object rolling slowly for a long period of time consuming network bandwidth.
cues.zh: 问题在于，如果有个物体在山上，一个相对陡峭的山坡，人造摩擦力会对抗重力，让物体长时间缓慢滚动，持续消耗网络带宽。

cues.en: Still not that relevant to the game so we didn't really want this behavior.
cues.zh: 这和游戏还是没太大关系，所以我们并不想要这种行为。

cues.en: So we went into the item code and the physics code and we implemented this fake friction system.
cues.zh: 所以我们深入物品代码和物理代码，实现了这套假摩擦系统。

cues.en: Totally arbitrary gameplay code, no one really understood why it was there except the network encoders, but it's this crazy thing where designers can say, oh yeah, please apply this friction curve over time so that we allow objects to travel down steep hills at full speed without applying any friction to them whatsoever, so they're just subject to Newtonian physics.
cues.zh: 完全是随意的玩法代码，除了网络编码器，没人真正明白它为什么存在。但这个东西很离谱：设计师可以说，行，请随时间应用这条摩擦曲线，这样我们就能让物体全速冲下陡坡，完全不给它们施加摩擦力，让它们只受牛顿物理支配。

cues.en: Once they reach a relatively gentle slope, we apply this friction curve that designers specify which
cues.zh: 一旦它们到达相对平缓的斜坡，我们就应用设计师指定的摩擦曲线，这条曲线

cues.en: starts with low friction and ramps up over the course of three to four seconds to infinite friction
cues.zh: 一开始摩擦力很低，在三到四秒内逐渐升高到无限大摩擦

cues.en: and brings them to a screeching halt.
cues.zh: 让它们戛然而止。

cues.en: So grenades dropped on hills would fly down them in a couple seconds
cues.zh: 所以扔在山坡上的手雷，几秒钟内就会冲下坡

cues.en: looking better in the process if I do say so myself
cues.zh: 而且恕我直言，这个过程看起来还更好了

cues.en: and then come to rest. Nobody noticed this. Nobody on the design team cared. Nobody on the sandbox team cared. But this probably saves another 10%
cues.zh: 然后停下来。没人注意到这一点。设计团队没人在意。沙盒团队也没人在意。但这大概又省了 10%

cues.en: just because there's so many items. Players drop so much stuff and it gets disturbed so often.
cues.zh: 因为物品太多了。玩家会丢下大量东西，而且这些东西经常被扰动。

cues.en: Next example, ragdoll networking. Ragdolls are kind of a pain.
cues.zh: 下一个例子，布娃娃系统的网络同步。布娃娃系统挺让人头疼的。

cues.en: They're deeply, deep physical simulations. They have a lot of nodes that move around.
cues.zh: 它们是极其深度的物理模拟。有很多节点在不断移动。

cues.en: It's very hard to capture all of their state in a small package.
cues.zh: 要把它们的全部状态压缩成一个小数据包非常困难。

cues.en: Like if you have a guy who's alive and he's running around playing an animation, you can pretty much capture his state as current position, direction he's traveling, maybe the animation he's playing and you're done, like a 100 bits, Not that big of a deal. Ragdolls on the other hand is like, God, we've got to transmit all these bones, they're all physically separate, they can bounce off things independently, what a mess.
cues.zh: 比如说一个活着的角色在跑动、播放动画，你基本可以用当前位置、移动方向、可能还有正在播放的动画来捕获他的状态，大概一百来比特就搞定了，不算什么大问题。但布娃娃系统就不一样了，天哪，我们得传输所有骨骼，它们都是独立物理运算的，可以各自弹开，真是一团糟。

cues.en: So we always sort of come across, we always come up with different compromises trying to network less of like some subsections of ragdoll, it never looked that great. It burned a lot of bandwidth. So we said, hey,
cues.zh: 所以我们总是遇到这个问题，总是想出各种折中方案，尽量减少布娃娃系统某些部分的网络传输，但效果一直不太理想，占用大量带宽。于是我们说，嘿，

cues.en: do we have to network rag dolls? Like really?
cues.zh: 我们真的非得对布娃娃系统做网络同步吗？真的有必要吗？

cues.en: So we're trying to turn the problem on its head and say, can we just get rid of this whole problem?
cues.zh: 所以我们试着换个角度想问题，能不能干脆把这个麻烦彻底去掉？

cues.en: And we brought this over to our Sandbox Design lead,
cues.zh: 我们把这个想法带给了沙盒设计负责人，

cues.en: Sage Merrill.
cues.zh: Sage Merrill。

cues.en: He said hey can we not network ragdolls? And we went through the three stages
cues.zh: 他说，嘿，我们能不能不对布娃娃系统做网络同步？然后我们经历了三个阶段

cues.en: of
cues.zh: 就是

cues.en: gameplay design
cues.zh: 游戏玩法设计

cues.en: response to this sort of thing which you'll probably see yourselves.
cues.zh: 对这类提议的典型反应，你们自己大概也会遇到。

cues.en: First shock,
cues.zh: 第一个阶段是震惊，

cues.en: what are you doing? Not network rag dolls. We might want to do something with them someday.
cues.zh: 你在干什么？不对布娃娃做网络同步？我们以后可能还想用它们做点什么啊。

cues.en: Then skepticism,
cues.zh: 然后是怀疑：

cues.en: are you sure this will work? Like that seems sort of crazy, doesn't everybody else network ragdolls?
cues.zh: “你确定这能行？听起来有点疯狂，其他人不都对布娃娃做网络同步吗？”

cues.en: And then consideration,
cues.zh: 接着是深入考量，

cues.en: where they dig in and tell us what
cues.zh: 他们开始仔细研究并告诉我们，

cues.en: really are the problems with not networking ragdolls for real.
cues.zh: 不对布娃娃做网络同步到底会带来哪些实际问题。

cues.en: And they came up with two things.
cues.zh: 他们找出了两点。

cues.en: First,
cues.zh: 第一，

cues.en: rag dolls block bullets.
cues.zh: 布娃娃会挡子弹。

cues.en: Like every other object in our game, rag dolls are physically real and they can block bullet trajectories.
cues.zh: 就像游戏里的其他物体一样，布娃娃具有真实的物理属性，会阻挡子弹轨迹。

cues.en: So we needed to
cues.zh: 所以如果我们打算

cues.en: deal with this somehow if we were going let rag dolls desync because otherwise you'd have invisible objects blocking bullets on different piers.
cues.zh: 让布娃娃不同步，就必须想办法解决这个问题，否则不同对等端上就会出现隐形物体挡子弹的情况。

cues.en: Second problem was humping.
cues.zh: 第二个问题是蹲起嘲讽（humping）。

cues.en: Quite serious.
cues.zh: 非常严肃的问题。

cues.en: Since Halo one there has been this tradition
cues.zh: 从 Halo 一代开始，社区里就一直有这个传统，

cues.en: in the Halo community, this tradition that we didn't want to mess with. When you kill someone
cues.zh: 这是个我们绝不想打破的传统。当你击杀某人后，

cues.en: and you have some time to spare because you're not under attack right now, walk over to their corpse
cues.zh: 由于暂时没遭到攻击，你有点闲暇时间，就会走到他的尸体旁，

cues.en: and then you press your crouch button dropping down like this
cues.zh: 然后按下蹲键，像这样蹲下去，

cues.en: and you release your crouch button and you push it again
cues.zh: 接着松开蹲键，再按一次，

cues.en: and so forth until you get bored.
cues.zh: 如此循环往复，直到你觉得无聊。

cues.en: Very important for the rag doll to be in the right spot so that humiliates him properly so that he can see that you're doing this to him.
cues.zh: 布娃娃必须处于正确的位置，这非常重要，这样才能恰如其分地羞辱对方，让他清楚看到你正在对他做什么。

cues.en: Totally serious.
cues.zh: 绝没开玩笑。

cues.en: This is a real thing.
cues.zh: 这真的是个很严肃的事。

cues.en: So we made two fixes to deal with these two problems. First,
cues.zh: 针对这两个问题，我们做了两项修复。第一，

cues.en: we went into our collision system and our projectile system and we allowed bullets and grenades to penetrate rag dolls freely. We allowed them to over penetrate without any side effects. We use a debug harness to verify that there were no side effects. It was added fairly late in the game.
cues.zh: 我们修改了碰撞系统和投射物系统，允许子弹和手雷自由穿透布娃娃。我们让它们完全过穿且不产生任何副作用。我们还使用了一个 debug harness 来验证确实没有副作用。这项功能是在游戏开发相当后期才加进来的。

cues.en: Second,
cues.zh: 第二，

cues.en: we have an assistant to synchronize the initial state of rag dolls. So we wouldn't network them over time as they were flying through the air bouncing around on the ground, but we would network them very exactly
cues.zh: 我们有一个辅助机制来同步布娃娃的初始状态。这样就不用在它们飞在空中、在地上弹跳的过程中持续联网同步，而是会非常精确地同步它们

cues.en: with a debug harness to verify. We would network their initial state
cues.zh: 并用调试工具来验证。我们会同步它们的初始状态

cues.en: at the moment of death on all boxes and all boxes would be guaranteed to start with that. Which meant as long as you didn't interfere with the rag doll too much, it would be in perfect sync in most cases.
cues.zh: 也就是所有机器上死亡瞬间的状态，并保证所有机器都从该状态开始。这意味着只要你不怎么干扰布娃娃，大多数情况下它都能保持完美同步。

cues.en: And this worked well enough. Once in a while if there's enough grenades going off, can have ragdolls just completely desync and it becomes obvious. But by and large, worked quite well.
cues.zh: 这套方案效果还不错。偶尔如果有足够多的手雷爆炸，布娃娃会完全失去同步，而且很明显。但总体来看，效果相当好。

cues.en: And we saved up another 10%,
cues.zh: 我们又节省了 10%，

cues.en: 12% of bandwidth maybe.
cues.zh: 也许 12% 的带宽。

cues.en: Lastly, have sort of a bucket of interesting cases of smoothing out bursts of bandwidth, smoothing out worst cases, very much like smoothing out worst case frames of CPU performance.
cues.zh: 最后，还有一堆有趣的案例，涉及平滑带宽突发、平滑最坏情况，很像平滑 CPU 性能中的最坏帧。

cues.en: First, we had problems with high rate of fire weapons, machine guns.
cues.zh: 首先，我们在高射速武器、机枪上遇到了问题。

cues.en: Bullets were networked optimally but not the damage that they were causing.
cues.zh: 子弹的网络同步是最优的，但它们造成的伤害却不是。

cues.en: People who designed the original machine gun networking knew that they would fire very rapidly and so they needed an efficient bit of networking for them. So they did that but when the bullets hit targets and dealt damage, it would trigger individual events for every bit of damage and that could take all your bandwidth very, very quickly if people with, if multiple people with machine guns were shooting targets with a lot of hit points.
cues.zh: 最初设计机枪网络同步的人知道机枪射速很快，所以需要为它们做高效的网络同步。他们确实做到了，但当子弹命中目标并造成伤害时，每一小点伤害都会触发单独事件；如果多个拿机枪的人射击高生命值目标，这会非常非常快地吃光你的带宽。

cues.en: So we went in and we said okay, for bullets that do a small amount of damage, we're going to just let clients predict some of those damage effects so that the host doesn't have to tell them, oh yeah, this kind of spark occurred and this sound played and yada yada yada. It's a machine gun, it's firing 15 times a second. Just play your own sparks.
cues.zh: 于是我们介入并决定，对于伤害很小的子弹，就让客户端自行预测其中一些伤害效果，这样主机就不必告诉它们“哦对，出现了这种火花、播放了这个声音”之类的。机枪每秒开火15次，就自己播放火花吧。

cues.en: Another example, had periodic update of game statistics data. So we have this blob of data we send that shows up on the end game stats.
cues.zh: 另一个例子是游戏统计数据的周期性更新。我们会发送一大块数据，显示在游戏结束统计里。

cues.en: It took priority over gameplay traffic
cues.zh: 它的优先级高于游戏玩法流量

cues.en: because it was on a protocol below our application layers. This would come in every like ten to thirty seconds and just take all the bandwidth in every packet until it was updated.
cues.zh: 因为它位于应用层之下的协议上。它大约每10到30秒来一次，在更新完成前会占满每个数据包的全部带宽。

cues.en: Two, three, four packets.
cues.zh: 两、三、四个数据包。

cues.en: And we discovered this with the bandwidth profiler because we get lag events during that time because at the end of that three or four frame period the networking would turn back on for the game and everything would warp
cues.zh: 我们通过带宽分析器发现了这一点，因为那段时间会出现卡顿事件：在三到四帧的周期结束时，游戏的网络会重新开启，然后一切都会跳变

cues.en: and we dug into it with the per packet information in the profiler and discovered low and behold all the gameplay data is just missing from four or five packets.
cues.zh: 我们利用分析器里的逐包信息深入排查，结果发现，四五个数据包里的游戏玩法数据全都不见了。

cues.en: And so we found this guy and we beat him into submission.
cues.zh: 于是我们找到了这个家伙，把它彻底制服了。

cues.en: You can only send 10% of each packet maximum. Statistics data can be laced fine.
cues.zh: 每个数据包最多只能发送10%的统计数据。统计数据可以穿插发送，没问题。

cues.en: Lastly, low priority objects were getting updates in perfect sync.
cues.zh: 最后，低优先级对象竟然在完全同步地更新。

cues.en: This is an interesting problem. So our priority system ramps up the priority of objects over time to make sure that eventually the state data guarantee will be met. Eventually the most updated state will arrive.
cues.zh: 这是个挺有意思的问题。我们的优先级系统会随着时间推移提高对象的优先级，确保最终能达成状态同步的保证，让最新状态总能送达。

cues.en: Problem was if you had a lot of objects that were out far, far away and they all tied for lowest priority and all they got disturbed at the same time like a pile of crates across the level that gets bumped into.
cues.zh: 问题是，如果远处有大量对象，它们都是最低优先级，而且同时被触动了——比如关卡另一头被撞倒的一堆箱子。

cues.en: They would all get lowest priority, they wouldn't get sent and they'd ramp up in priority slowly, slowly, slowly, slowly and then they'd all get really old and then they'd all panic on the same frame and say, oh crap, we haven't been sent in five seconds, we need to get in sync.
cues.zh: 它们起初都是最低优先级，根本发不出去，优先级就慢慢、慢慢地往上涨，直到数据严重过时，然后全在同一帧“慌了神”说：糟糕，我们都 5 秒没发送了，必须立刻同步。

cues.en: And they would eat two packets
cues.zh: 于是它们一下子占满了两个数据包，

cues.en: to say, oh my god, this whole stack of crates over here just got updated. And all the guy, the guy you're standing in front of, guy you're fighting, didn't get any bandwidth during those two because he wasn't panicked. He got an update recently and so we got lag artifacts from this.
cues.zh: 光用来同步“天啊，这边整整一堆箱子刚被碰了”。而你眼前正交战的对手在这两个包里根本分不到带宽，因为他还没到“恐慌”状态，最近刚更新过，这就导致了卡顿现象。

cues.en: Simple fix again,
cues.zh: 解决办法依然很简单，

cues.en: limit objects that can take this panic priority to a fixed number per packet. So we always reserve space in the packet
cues.zh: 限制每个数据包中能获得这种“恐慌优先级”的对象数量。这样我们就能在数据包里始终预留空间，

cues.en: To answer your question specifically, yes, vehicle updates are a huge amount of bandwidth because they are huge, they're highly noticeable, players care about them a lot, they catch the eye. In Halo three we spent a lot of perf on them.
cues.zh: 具体回答你的问题：是的，载具更新会占用大量带宽，因为数据量很大、非常显眼，玩家很在意，也很抓眼球。在 Halo 3 里，我们在这上面花了很多性能。

cues.en: In Reach we actually had a major development initiative to fix that and I can talk about that because we have few more minutes. It's pretty interesting.
cues.zh: 在 Reach 里，我们其实有一个重要的开发计划来解决这个问题；还有几分钟，我可以讲讲。挺有意思的。

cues.en: So in Halo three we had a blending system which we use on bipeds. So when you got a network update about a biped and it was out of sync by
cues.zh: 在 Halo 3 里，我们有一个用在双足单位上的混合系统。所以当你收到一个双足单位的网络更新，它不同步了

cues.en: some amount, some number of feet and you had to sort of fix up, get in sync with the host, We did this visual only interpolation that I mentioned with assassinations where
cues.zh: 一定量，若干英尺，你得把它修正过来，和主机同步。我们做了我提到过的、用在刺杀上的纯视觉插值，也就是

cues.en: your logical state warps and your physics state warps to that location but your body gets this little blend, this little exponential blend that consumes the error as you continue to predict forward. So it looks pretty good.
cues.zh: 你的逻辑状态和物理状态会瞬移到那个位置，但你的身体会做一点混合，一点指数混合，在你继续向前预测时消耗掉误差。所以看起来还不错。

cues.en: For vehicles,
cues.zh: 对于载具，

cues.en: we couldn't do this in Halo three because of their interaction with Havoc.
cues.zh: 我们在 Halo 3 里做不到，因为它们和 Havoc 的交互。

cues.en: Blending
cues.zh: 混合

cues.zh: 因为它在 Havoc 中的表示方式，还因为一些烦人的问题，比如

cues.en: contact points of the wheels on the ground. So when you warp the physics, all the dirt starts coming up from the new locations and the fact that you're blending this object to it looks like garbage, like you're clearly cheating.
cues.zh: 也就是车轮在地面上的接触点。所以当你瞬移物理状态时，所有尘土会从新位置扬起，而你又在混合这个对象，看起来就一团糟，明显像在作弊。

cues.en: So for
cues.zh: 所以对于

cues.en: Reach we rewrote that system,
cues.zh: Reach，我们重写了那个系统，

cues.en: that visual interpolation system to work with all object types. We fixed all the issues with vehicles so we would calculate the transform from
cues.zh: 让那个视觉插值系统适用于所有对象类型。我们修复了车辆相关的所有问题，这样我们就能从……计算变换

cues.en: the visual object to the real physics object and the inverse of that and we would use that to move things around as needed so any visual element
cues.zh: 把视觉对象与真实的物理对象相互映射，我们会根据需要用它来移动物体，这样任何视觉元素

cues.en: like a dirt from a wheel would get blended back to the visual position
cues.zh: 就像车轮甩出的泥土会被混合回视觉位置一样

cues.en: to correspond with the visual mesh being blended.
cues.zh: 以对应正在混合的视觉网格。

cues.en: The result of that is that we could cut down our vehicle update rates a lot. On Halo three we tried very, very hard to keep vehicles at 20 updates a second, rarely below 15 because they were very high priorities how we did that,
cues.zh: 结果是，我们可以大幅降低载具的更新频率。在 Halo 3 中，我们非常非常努力地把载具保持在每秒 20 次更新，很少低于 15 次，因为它们的优先级非常高；我们就是这么做的，

cues.en: because they looked really bad when they warped because we didn't have any blending. With this blending, we found we could drop vehicles to
cues.zh: 因为它们变形时看起来非常糟，因为我们没有做任何混合。有了这种混合，我们发现可以把载具投放至

cues.en: anywhere down to like five updates a second and they would look good.
cues.zh: 低到每秒大约五次更新，效果也都不错。

cues.zh: 对象的逻辑位置会立即被扭曲。Havoc 表示、所有刚体和物体都会立即被扭曲，

cues.zh: 让我先说完，再回到那个问题。视觉表示，以及我们所说的碰撞表示，

cues.en: which is distinct from physics, are blended. And the collision representation is all the things that can be shot.
cues.zh: 它与物理系统不同，并被混合在一起。而碰撞表示则涵盖所有可被射击的对象。

cues.en: So if you shoot a guy who's blending and you see it hit his body, it will actually do damage. It will work correctly.
cues.zh: 所以如果你射击一个正在插值平滑的玩家，并且看到击中了他，那确实会造成伤害，一切运转正常。

cues.en: So the thing I was saying about physics, the reason we have to warp physics is because you can have this case with like a thin wall and you're predicting that you're running on the right side of the wall and then you get an update that says, oh no, you're on the left side of the wall and this is a solid wall but fairly thin.
cues.zh: 关于我刚才提到的物理系统，我们之所以必须对物理进行瞬移拉回，是因为可能会遇到薄墙的情况：你预测自己在墙的右侧跑，接着收到更新说，噢不，你在墙的左侧，而这堵实体墙相当薄。

cues.en: If you try to blend physics and not warp it,
cues.zh: 如果你尝试对物理做平滑过渡而不是直接瞬移，

cues.en: it's very hard to get that to sort of consistently, well won't look right. Haddock will predict all sorts of terrible things as you push the rigid body through the wall, right? It'll start exploding.
cues.zh: 就很难保证表现一致，视觉上看起来会不对劲。当你把刚体硬生生穿墙推过去时，Havok 会预测出各种可怕的结果，对吧？它就会开始疯狂报错乱飞。

cues.en: So we warp havoc and the logical position to the other side of the wall so prediction can be happy and you know, think I'm on the right spot, everything's cool and then you get this visual only blend, visual and collision blend. That's
cues.zh: 所以我们会直接把 Havok 和逻辑位置瞬移到墙的另一边，让预测系统顺畅运行，觉得“我在正确的位置，一切安好”，然后只做纯视觉的平滑过渡，视觉和碰撞的混合过渡。这——

cues.en: great. Nobody's behind you.
cues.zh: 太棒了，没人排在你后面了。

cues.en: a very good question. When you are driving a vehicle in Halo, you have the same level of control over it that you would normally have over your own biped.
cues.zh: 非常好的问题。当你在 Halo 里驾驶载具时，你对它的控制程度和你平时控制双足角色完全一样。

cues.en: So the way that works for the biped is as you're running around, you transmit your world space position and orientation and other things to the host and he sort of copes with it. He applies the same blending logic that clients use unless it's insane and then of course he'll correct you. Vehicles work the same way. As soon as you get into the driver's seat of a vehicle, your
cues.zh: 双足角色的运作方式是，当你在四周跑动时，会把世界空间下的位置、朝向等数据同步给主机，主机会处理这些数据。它会应用和客户端一样的平滑混合逻辑，除非数据太离谱，那主机当然会纠正你。载具也是同理。一旦你坐进载具的驾驶座，你的——

cues.en: control stream switches. Instead of sending your biped data, it sends your vehicle data, the host copes with it, everyone blends all the way around and everything looks beautiful. And yeah, there's no latency whatsoever.
cues.zh: 控制数据流就会切换。它不再发送双足角色的数据，而是发送载具数据，主机负责处理，所有人全方位进行平滑插值，看起来就非常自然。而且没错，完全感觉不到任何延迟。

cues.en: Client isn't actually authoritative technically because he can be corrected, but he's authoritative within his bubble.
cues.zh: 客户端从技术上讲其实并不具有权威性，因为它可以被纠正，但在自己的小圈子里它就是权威。
